title: Prove the terminal answering path works with no factory and no network
description:
WRITE THE GUARD BEFORE THE CHANGE, so it proves the change did not break it — not after, when it can only describe what survived.

The product line this whole extraction draws: terminal answering is ticks and works offline; phone answering is a cloud feature and needs the cloud. Phase 4b removes the local Telegram transport, and the risk is that it takes something else with it.

Pin the offline path: an agent parks a question (cmd/tk/cmd/herd_wait.go:209 shows the no-channel branch — 'parked for terminal answer with tk answer <id> <answer>'), and a human resolves it with tk answer / tk approve / tk reject, with NO channel configured, NO factory deployed and NO network. That path uses the question store (internal/operator/*.go) which STAYS; only the transport leaves.

Cover the shape end to end rather than a unit: park, list, resolve, and confirm the resolution reaches the agent. Assert it works with the operator channel entirely unconfigured, since that is the state a terminal-only user is permanently in.

If any part of the offline path turns out to already depend on the Telegram transport, that is the most valuable thing you can find — report it loudly, because it changes the shape of the deletion tick.
acceptance_criteria: A test proves park -> resolve -> agent-notified works with no channel configured and no network. It fails if the offline path regresses. Any existing dependency of the terminal path on internal/operator/telegram is reported rather than worked around. go test ./... green.
closed_reason: Completed: 207-line offline guard proving park -> answer -> notify works with no channel, no factory, no network — AND it found the escape hatch it was written to look for: tk ask/answer fell back through factoryOperatorChannel() to the real ~/.ticksrc and made live HTTPS calls to a deployed Worker with a real bearer token. RESULT committed by the orchestrator after the fact; the brief never said the report was the deliverable.
